newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Growth seen for foreign builders in Dutch market.
newsitem.headline: Growth seen for foreign builders in Dutch market.

text.p: Non-Dutch builders have a market share of only one percent in the Netherlands but hefty growth prospects lie ahead, a study for the Dutch Housing Ministry said on Wednesday.
"It is estimated that 12 to 22 percent of Dutch construction projects could be attractive for foreign, internationally-active building companies and consultancies," the ministry said in a statement.
The one percent market share has a value of about 600 million guilders. More than half of this is generated through large projects such as power and water purification plants.
The ministry said growth prospects for non-Dutch builders were seen in building chemical plants, oil refineries, bridges, ports, tunnels and high-speed train links.
Of the surrounding countries, only large Belgian construction firms had applied a structural strategy to gain a market share in the Netherlands.

One of the conclusions of the study is that a more open Dutch construction market will offer more advantages for Dutch companies than the more closed market which existed until recently, the ministry said.
